```{r setup}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| error: false
#| results: 'hide'

# Load dashboardr (includes dplyr, highcharter as dependencies)
library(dashboardr)

# Global chunk options
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  error = FALSE,
  fig.width = 12,
  fig.height = 8,
  dpi = 300
)

# Bundle loader — reads the RDS bundle once, then extracts datasets by key
.load_bundle <- function(bundle_file, key) {
  if (!exists('.dashboardr_bundle_cache', inherits = FALSE))
    .dashboardr_bundle_cache <<- list()
  if (is.null(.dashboardr_bundle_cache[[bundle_file]]))
    .dashboardr_bundle_cache[[bundle_file]] <<- readRDS(bundle_file)
  if (!(key %in% names(.dashboardr_bundle_cache[[bundle_file]])))
    stop("Bundle key '", key, "' not found in ", bundle_file, call. = FALSE)
  .dashboardr_bundle_cache[[bundle_file]][[key]]
}

# Load multiple datasets

# Load wp2
wp2 <- .load_bundle('dashboard_data_bundle.rds', 'wp2_151obs.rds')
cat('wp2 loaded:', nrow(wp2), 'rows,', ncol(wp2), 'columns\n')

# Load domains_long
domains_long <- .load_bundle('dashboard_data_bundle.rds', 'domains_long_330obs.rds')
cat('domains_long loaded:', nrow(domains_long), 'rows,', ncol(domains_long), 'columns\n')

# Load problems_long
problems_long <- .load_bundle('dashboard_data_bundle.rds', 'problems_long_236obs.rds')
cat('problems_long loaded:', nrow(problems_long), 'rows,', ncol(problems_long), 'columns\n')

# Load outcomes_long
outcomes_long <- .load_bundle('dashboard_data_bundle.rds', 'outcomes_long_235obs.rds')
cat('outcomes_long loaded:', nrow(outcomes_long), 'rows,', ncol(outcomes_long), 'columns\n')

# Load problems_report
problems_report <- .load_bundle('dashboard_data_bundle.rds', 'problems_report_6obs.rds')
cat('problems_report loaded:', nrow(problems_report), 'rows,', ncol(problems_report), 'columns\n')

# Load outcomes_report
outcomes_report <- .load_bundle('dashboard_data_bundle.rds', 'outcomes_report_7obs.rds')
cat('outcomes_report loaded:', nrow(outcomes_report), 'rows,', ncol(outcomes_report), 'columns\n')

# Load runtime_report
runtime_report <- .load_bundle('dashboard_data_bundle.rds', 'runtime_report_4obs.rds')
cat('runtime_report loaded:', nrow(runtime_report), 'rows,', ncol(runtime_report), 'columns\n')

```

## Which problems are addressed?


The majority of interventions address the problem of **cybercrime** (36%): reducing the risk of fraud, scams or impersonation, promoting protective measures against cyberattacks targeting SMEs, or resilience trainings for vulnerable groups such as seniors. Many of these interventions are initiated by the Centre for Crime Prevention and Safety (CCV) or the police.

The second most important problem concerns the **safety and wellbeing of youth** (21%), such as cyberbullying, online hate, violations of online sexual boundaries, social media addiction and problematic phone use. These are followed by **AI and digital transformation** (14%), **digital inclusion** (10%), **digital literacy** (10%) and **misinformation, news and media literacy** (6.4%).


::: {.panel-tabset}

### {{< iconify ph chart-bar-horizontal-fill >}} Problems addressed


```{r problems-report}
# Problem addressed (inductive coding, % of interventions)
result <- viz_bar(
  data = problems_report,
  title = "Problem addressed (inductive coding, % of interventions)",
  horizontal = TRUE,
  x_var = "category",
  y_var = "pct",
  x_order = c("Cybercrime", "Safety and wellbeing of youth", "AI and digital transformation", "Digital inclusion", "Digital literacy", "Misinformation, news and media literacy"),
  color_palette = "#3D7271",
  x_label = "",
  y_label = "% of interventions",
  tooltip_suffix = "%"
)

# Set chart height
if (inherits(result, 'highchart')) {
  result <- highcharter::hc_size(result, height = 440)
}

# Force container height with explicit wrapper
result <- htmltools::div(
  style = 'height: 440px !important; min-height: 440px !important; width: 100%; overflow: visible;',
  result
)

result
```

*Source: final report 'Grip op Digitaal Burgerschap' (inductive coding of the problem, outcome and runtime descriptions).*



### {{< iconify ph bank-fill >}} Policy questions



In addition, we coded which policy questions from the Digital Society policy framework each intervention addresses (up to three per intervention).

```{r problems-policy}
# Policy questions addressed (max. 3 per intervention)
result <- viz_bar(
  data = problems_long,
  title = "Policy questions addressed (max. 3 per intervention)",
  horizontal = TRUE,
  bar_type = "count",
  x_var = "category",
  sort_by_value = TRUE,
  color_palette = "#3D7271",
  x_label = "",
  y_label = "Number of interventions"
)

result
```


:::

## What do interventions aim to achieve?


Overall, the interventions largely expect to make citizens more digitally skilled and secure, which closely corresponds to the problems they seek to address. 34% expect **improved online security** via reduced vulnerability to cybercrime, fraud and phishing; 30% aim to **promote digital literacy** (basic skills, media literacy, AI literacy); and 21% specifically target the **digital safety and health of youth**. Fewer interventions focus on access to digital devices and services (8%), responsible digitalisation within organisations (4%) and broader social risks such as public disorder or road safety (2%). For 1%, no concrete outcome is stated.


::: {.panel-tabset}
